displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that reasons-responsive capacities justify regulation and evaluation but cannot establish ultimate moral desert unless the agent authors the standards and dispositions producing action.

novelty.explanation: This combines Harris's causal-source and practical-regulation distinctions into a narrower, proportionate thesis about ultimate desert.

premises.text: Higher-level descriptions can be causally useful and genuinely explanatory while remaining entirely dependent on constitutive conditions the described agent neither selected nor ultimately controlled.

novelty.explanation: This accepts macro-level explanation while repairing the earlier inference that neural dependence automatically eliminates every form of control.

premises.text: A person's sensitivity to reasons can justify protection, deterrence, rehabilitation, and prospective expectations without establishing backward-looking desert grounded in ultimate self-creation.

novelty.explanation: This develops the conceded practical functions while restricting the nonauthorship conclusion to ultimate desert.

premises.text: If luck excuses diminished competence because relevant capacities were not adequately available, constitutive luck also requires explanation when those capacities are unusually strong or socially rewarded.

novelty.explanation: This replaces the golfer analogy with a more general symmetry challenge concerning favorable and unfavorable constitutive luck.

premises.text: Neural prediction challenges authorship only when it reliably tracks complex choices before the agent-level deliberative process begins, not merely before conscious awareness of its conclusion.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the discriminating experimental condition missing from the transcript's hypothetical prediction argument.

conclusion.text: Therefore compatibilist competence can remain practically indispensable while ultimate desert and self-origination remain unsupported by either deterministic causation or indeterministic variation.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion preserves Harris's central dilemma while expressly retaining the practical value of compatibilist capacities.

newArguments.title: The Symmetry of Constitutive Luck
newArguments.text: Responsibility practices already reduce blame when injury, coercion, deprivation, or developmental impairment weakens reasons-responsive capacities. Favorable constitutive conditions should be analyzed by the same principle: unusually effective self-control also depends on opportunities, temperament, education, and neural organization the person did not originate. This does not erase practical distinctions between agents. It instead weakens claims that unequal moral desert tracks capacities whose distribution is substantially fortuitous.

novelty.explanation: This is a new distributive symmetry argument linking favorable and unfavorable constitutive luck without relying on another transcript move.

newArguments.title: Two Responsibility Ledgers
newArguments.text: Separate a prospective ledger from a desert ledger. The prospective ledger records who can understand reasons, comply with rules, repair harm, and respond to incentives; it supports calibrated accountability. The desert ledger asks whether suffering is deserved simply because the wrongdoer ultimately authored the source of wrongdoing. Causal nonauthorship leaves the first ledger intact while undermining the second. This division preserves governance without allowing institutional usefulness to settle the metaphysical question by definition.

novelty.explanation: This new framework formalizes two distinct justificatory tasks and prevents practical accountability from being mistaken for ultimate desert.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that free will consists in temporally extended, reasons-responsive self-governance sufficient for reciprocal accountability, not exemption from causation or complete authorship of one's origins.

novelty.explanation: This unifies Dennett's competence, macro-control, and pragmatic responsibility moves into a single bounded thesis.

premises.text: Control is meaningful when outcomes systematically vary with an agent's reasons, attention, commitments, and corrective capacities rather than with coercion, compulsion, or disabling impairment.

novelty.explanation: This specifies control through counterfactual sensitivity and contrasts functioning agency with recognized impairments.

premises.text: A process can belong to an agent when it is integrated with memory, commitments, learning, and self-correction across time, even though its neural implementation is unconscious.

novelty.explanation: This develops the macro-authorship reply by supplying concrete criteria for agent-level integration.

premises.text: Consequentialist accountability is legitimate only when it is proportionate, evidence-sensitive, revisable, and calibrated to competence, thereby excluding indiscriminate punishment and absolute desert.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the stable-enforcement argument by adding explicit ethical and epistemic constraints on institutional consequences.

premises.text: The relevant ability to do otherwise is reliable performance across nearby circumstances where reasons or opportunities vary, because deliberation evaluates capacities rather than impossible universal replays.

novelty.explanation: This defines relevant similarity more carefully and avoids simply declaring exact physical replay irrelevant.

conclusion.text: Therefore causally embedded agents can possess a limited but genuine freedom that supports proportionate accountability whenever integrated capacities allow understanding, deliberation, correction, and dependable response to reasons.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion integrates bounded control, limited self-authorship, and constrained accountability without claiming absolute responsibility.

newArguments.title: Attributive Integration Test
newArguments.text: Authorship should be tested by integration rather than conscious micro-initiation. An action is attributable when its generating process is connected to the person's memories, standing commitments, learned skills, evaluative dispositions, and capacity for later correction. Prediction before awareness does not defeat authorship if the predictor reads that integrated process. By contrast, coercion, seizure, manipulation, or dissociation can break the relevant connections. This test makes macro-authorship discriminating rather than merely metaphorical.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a structured attribution test answering prediction and manipulation objections beyond the transcript's illustrative examples.

newArguments.title: Reciprocal Normative Standing
newArguments.text: Responsibility is not only a technique for changing behavior; it is also a reciprocal practice among agents capable of offering reasons, recognizing claims, apologizing, making commitments, and repairing harm. Those capacities create a form of normative standing even when nobody authored their original endowment. Institutions should scale demands to actual competence and opportunity. This relational basis explains why accountability can respect persons rather than treating them simply as mechanisms to be managed.

novelty.explanation: This is a new relational argument supplementing consequentialism with reciprocal reason-giving and person-respecting constraints.
